claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid and compositionally homogeneous, including at their surfaces.
Cu is a lower-melting constituent of FeNiCrCoCu and is the most likely element to segregate during heating.
Temperature-induced surface segregation governs the onset and progression of the FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle phase transition.
Elevated temperature preferentially drives Cu atoms from the nanoparticle interior to the surface.
Surface enrichment in Cu reduces the local surface melting point.
The reduced local melting point initiates premelting at the nanoparticle surface.
Surface premelting propagates inward and controls progression to complete melting.
A surface passivation layer can inhibit surface atomic mobility and thereby reduce segregation.
The controlled comparison is between as-prepared nanoparticles and otherwise comparable surface-passivated nanoparticles.
As-prepared nanoparticles will begin surface premelting at a lower temperature than passivated nanoparticles.
Cu surface enrichment will coincide temporally with the first TEM or DSC signatures of melting.
The proposed mechanism applies near the premelting regime, where surface atomic mobility is sufficiently activated.
Grain-boundary diffusion or pre-existing compositional heterogeneity may also influence melting behavior.
Similar premelting onset temperatures and nearly identical surface-composition profiles in passivated and as-prepared particles would falsify the segregation-driven hypothesis.
